A.explanation: Gives the correct $220 \text{ V}$ across the floodlights but $2000 \text{ W}$ is too small for $P = VI$ with $10 \text{ A}$.

B.explanation: Total cable drop is $20 \text{ V}$, leaving $220 \text{ V}$ for the floodlights, so $P = 220 \times 10 = 2200 \text{ W}$.

C.explanation: Uses only one $1 \Omega$ cable so subtracts only $10 \text{ V}$ to get $230 \text{ V}$, ignoring the return cable.

D.explanation: Subtracts only $10 \text{ V}$ for one cable to get $230 \text{ V}$ and then calculates $P = 230 \times 10 = 2300 \text{ W}$.

hints: Notice the two cables are in series with the floodlights, with $1 \Omega + 1 \Omega = 2 \Omega$ total and the same $10 \text{ A}$ through them.
Connect the $10 \text{ A}$ current to the p.d. lost in the cables using $V = IR$ for the total $2 \Omega$ resistance.
Connect the remaining p.d. at the floodlights to the delivered power using $P = VI$ with the $10 \text{ A}$ current.
walkthrough: Identify the series loop: the $10 \text{ A}$ from the $240 \text{ V}$ generator passes through the outgoing $1 \Omega$ cable, the floodlights, then the return $1 \Omega$ cable.
State the loss rule: p.d. is lost in the cables according to $V_{lost} = IR$, using total cable resistance $R = 1 + 1 = 2 \Omega$.
Substitute values with units: $V_{lost} = 10 \text{ A} \times 2 \Omega = 20 \text{ V}$.
Subtract from the supply to find the floodlight p.d.: $V = 240 \text{ V} - 20 \text{ V} = 220 \text{ V}$.
Calculate delivered power with $P = VI$ at the floodlights: $P = 220 \text{ V} \times 10 \text{ A} = 2200 \text{ W}$.
Check units and options: $V$ in $\text{V}$ and $P$ in $\text{W}$ match $220 \text{ V}$ and $2200 \text{ W}$. This is option B.
